register.problem: English 'to do a favor' is a calque; English only uses it ditransitively ('do someone a favor')
'veinte años de edad' is textbook filler; natives just say 'Tengo veinte años'
register.example: Tengo veinte años.

register.problem: 'cada noche' is a literal 'every night' calque; natives say 'todas las noches'
register.example: Mi abuela toma té verde todas las noches.
register.exampleEn: My grandmother drinks green tea every night.

register.problem: 'Nos dan la mesa' with definite article is unnatural at a restaurant; it's 'una mesa'
register.example: Nos dan una mesa junto a la ventana.
register.exampleEn: They give us a table next to the window.

register.problem: 'En el pedido escribimos...' is stilted; nobody writes down an order this way — 'nuestro pedido es' is the natural restaurant phrasing
register.example: Nuestro pedido es pollo con arroz.
register.exampleEn: Our order is chicken with rice.

register.problem: 'De bebida' is a 'for a drink' calque; natives say 'para beber'
register.example: Para beber, todos queremos jugo de naranja.
register.exampleEn: To drink, we all want orange juice.

register.problem: 'El techo tiene una lámpara' is an inanimate-'have' calque; Spanish uses 'hay' for fixtures (deck itself does: u11-014, u11-016)
register.example: En el techo hay una lámpara bonita.
register.exampleEn: There is a nice lamp on the ceiling.

register.problem: 'Debe girar a la derecha' is textbook deber+infinitivo; in real directions natives use the imperative
register.example: Gire a la derecha en la próxima esquina.
register.exampleEn: Turn right at the next corner.

register.problem: 'coche' is Peninsular; Latin-American everyday default is 'carro' (or 'auto' in the Southern Cone)
register.example: Mi carro está estacionado afuera.

register.problem: 'billete' is Peninsular; Latin America says 'boleto' (or 'pasaje')
register.example: Compré el boleto por internet.

register.problem: 'El sueldo es suficiente para vivir' is an English calque; natives use the verb 'alcanzar'
register.example: El sueldo me alcanza para vivir.
register.exampleEn: I earn enough to live on.

register.problem: 'hay mucho calor' — Spanish weather uses hacer, not hay; classroom treats 'hay calor' as an error/calque
register.example: En verano hace mucho calor aquí.

register.problem: 'El frío de la noche es fuerte' is a stiff textbook construction; natives say 'hace un frío...' idiom
register.example: Por la noche hace un frío muy fuerte.

register.problem: Generic singular 'las hojas del árbol' reads like a fable; in speech natives generalize with the plural
register.example: En otoño se caen las hojas de los árboles.

register.problem: 'La granja tiene muchos pollos' is an English-calque of 'the farm has'; natives say 'en la granja hay'
register.example: En la granja hay muchos pollos.

register.problem: 'produce lana' is bookish; everyday speech uses dar (las ovejas dan lana)
register.example: Las ovejas dan lana muy suave.

register.problem: regional mismatch: 'enfadado' is Peninsular; Latin-American default (deck rule) teaches 'enojado'
register.example: Está enojada porque llegué tarde.

register.problem: example has a tagged-on '..., você sabe?' calque of English 'Do you know...?'; classroom/natural form is 'Como é que você se chama?'
register.example: Como é que você se chama?

register.problem: 'Doze meses formam um ano' is a textbook aphorism nobody says unprompted; natural phrasing uses ter
register.example: Um ano tem doze meses.

register.problem: fronted 'Mil reais é o aluguel' is stiff inverted word order; natives say 'O aluguel é mil reais'
register.example: O aluguel é mil reais.

register.problem: 'para entrar ar' is a textbook calque; the spoken idiom is 'pra entrar um ar' (with article), and informal imperatives match the deck's other examples
register.example: Abre a janela pra entrar um ar, por favor?
register.exampleEn: Open the window for some air, please?

register.problem: 'no escritório aqui de casa' is awkward word order natives rarely use; 'o escritório de casa' (home office) is the natural way to express it
register.example: Trabalho no escritório de casa.
register.exampleEn: I work from my home office.

register.problem: 'Esfreguei o olho com areia' implies rubbing the eye WITH sand as the tool; natives say they rubbed it because sand was in the eye
register.example: Esfreguei o olho porque estava com areia.
register.exampleEn: I rubbed my eye because there was sand in it.

register.problem: exampleEn 'I'm not hearing you' is a Portuguese calque; natural English is 'I can't hear you'
register.example: Fale mais alto, não estou ouvindo.
register.exampleEn: Speak up, I can't hear you.
